name: 席恩
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:194
who: Xien, a human boy of the White Hill forest, a seventeen-year-old apprentice of the Mirror Lake poets and not yet a legend: about 172 cm, slender and light on his feet, wholly covered by his clothes. Long snow-white hair, white since the first days of his life, tied back at the nape with a plain leather cord; lake-grey-blue eyes that look steady and quiet, as if watching something at the bottom of water; a fine, delicate face with long narrow eyes and a small teardrop mole under the right eye (on the viewer's left when they face us). A thin, freshly healed vertical scar stands between his brows. A small fish-skin pouch holding a few birch-bark strips written with songs hangs at his belt. A light, quiet, clever air that gives nothing away. The small teardrop mole is under his RIGHT eye only, which is on the viewer's LEFT when he faces us; the skin under the other eye is clear. If the identity reference shows a mole on the other side, ignore that and put it on the viewer's left.
palette: snow white and frost grey-blue, moss green, deerskin brown, a little birch-bark pale
casual: His forest clothes: a knee-length short tunic of moss-green dyed wool with long fitted sleeves, a sleeveless deerskin jerkin over it, belted at the waist, close-fitting brown trousers and soft leather boots, the small fish-skin pouch at his belt. He stands light on his feet with the hands loose, a calm, level look.
private: Resting at the lake: a long-sleeved, high-collared undyed wool shirt in pale grey-green, plain wool trousers and soft leather boots, the white hair loose over one shoulder. He holds a birch-bark strip written with a song and reads it, a quiet look.
battle: Keeping watch at the city gate: the moss-green tunic and deerskin jerkin with leather bracers over the sleeves and tall laced boots. In both hands he grips a long white ash-wood spear with a frost-white tip, held forward and slightly up, the frost on the tip glittering; a wide-awake, unflinching look, the eyes open, the mouth closed.
formal: A guest in the great hall of the White Hill: his one good tunic of clean moss-green wool, laced at the throat with a thin hide thong instead of any buttons, a plain grey wool cloak pinned with a small bone clasp, a leather belt, soft leather boots, and a small pale frost-crystal charm hanging at the belt. He stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, a serious, polite look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the grey-blue eyes wide open and looking straight at the viewer, serious and quiet, the mouth closed, the thin upright scar between the brows clear. Cold pale lake light from one side and the warm glow of a torch from the other, lighting the snow-white hair. Foreground blur: drifting frost-white sparks and the tip of a frost-white spear.

name: 戈尔
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:250
who: Gol, a human, the forty-six-year-old head of the White Hill hunting band, a hero of the beast age: about 189 cm, broad-shouldered and long-armed, hard muscle, standing still like an old oak. Long iron-grey hair combed straight back, the temples shaved short. A black bear-hide patch covers his left eye (on the viewer's right when they face us); the right eye is a sharp hawk gold-brown. A hard, chiselled face with high cheekbones and a square jaw, and an old scar running from under the eye patch down to the corner of his mouth (on the viewer's right when they face us). Fair, clean skin. Still strikingly handsome for his age. A heavy, still, commanding air; the young ones fear him and secretly copy the way he walks. His one open eye (the right eye, on the viewer's left when he faces us) is a hawk's warm gold-brown, amber, NOT blue and NOT grey. He has exactly one scar on his face: it starts at the lower edge of the eye patch and runs down to the corner of his mouth, on the viewer's right; the forehead, the brow and the cheek on the open-eye side (viewer's left) are unscarred.
face: FACE, as in the references: a mature man's face of forty-six, hard and chiselled, high cheekbones, a square jaw, faint lines at the corner of the open right eye and across the brow; the right eye a sharp, narrow hawk gold-brown; a heavy straight iron-grey eyebrow; a firm, closed mouth. The scar runs from under the eye patch to the corner of the mouth on the viewer's right. Skin shadows are a soft warm tone. The open eye is gold-brown amber, not blue-grey; the single scar is on the eye-patch side only (viewer's right), nothing on the viewer's left.
build: 189 cm, broad-shouldered and long-armed, solid muscle all over, a barrel chest and thick forearms.
palette: iron grey, bear-hide black, hawk gold-brown, burnished copper, deep leather brown
casual: His hunting-lord clothes: a black bear-hide cloak thrown over one shoulder, under it a hide cuirass worked to a polish with a row of copper hunting-band buttons across the chest, dark wool trousers and high laced boots; a silver staff, its head notched on one side, in his right hand, held low at an angle. Two short spears hang from the belt at his waist. A calm, unhurried, hard look.
private: Resting after the hunt: the bear cloak and cuirass off, a loose undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow and the collar open, dark wool trousers and soft boots. He holds a clay cup in one hand, the black eye patch still in place, a tired, quiet look.
battle: Leading the hunt: the bear-hide cloak over the hide cuirass with its copper buttons, leather bracers, a bow carved all over with names slung across his back. He grips a long spear in both hands, braced and held forward at an angle, two short spears at the belt; the silver staff is left behind. A fierce, unflinching look, the jaw set.
formal: In the great hall of the White Hill: the polished hide cuirass worn under a clean black bear-hide cloak pinned with a heavy copper clasp, the iron-grey hair freshly combed back, the silver staff in his right hand. He stands upright like an old oak, the left hand resting on the belt, a stern, proud look.
art: A close portrait from slightly low, the one hawk-gold eye looking straight at the viewer with a hard, measuring look, as if testing with the point of a spear, the eye patch and the old scar clear, the lips closed. Warm low firelight from the left, cool dark behind. Foreground blur: drifting sparks and the edge of a bearskin cloak. He wears the bear-hide cloak over the polished cuirass.

name: 黎丝
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:307
who: Lis, a human woman of the Forest Sea, thirty-six, a retired huntress: about 172 cm, a tall, lean runner's frame. Short grey-white hair, gone grey in her thirties, with one long lock left across the forehead covering an old scar at the corner of the right eye (on the viewer's left when they face us). Deep forest-green eyes with the outer corners tilted up, a cold, sharp, beautiful face with thin lips that looks frosted when she does not smile and turns girlish when she does. Fair skin. A single white hair is wound round the back of her longbow, a child's hair she kept. A cold, silent, precise air, always judging how far away a deer is.
build: 172 cm, a huntress's long lean frame: strong long legs, a back and waist like a drawn bow, narrow shoulders, a slim waist and gently rounded hips, a C-cup.
palette: grey-white and forest green, deerskin dun, yew-wood brown, a little bone white
casual: Her hunting clothes: a close-fitting grey-green deerskin hunting shirt and trousers, the cuffs and trouser legs bound tight, thin soft slippers so thin the shape of her toes shows, a skinning knife at her belt. A yew longbow with a white hair wound round its back is slung across her back. She stands very still, one hand on the bow strap, a cool, level look.
private: At home in the hut: a long-sleeved, high-collared soft grey-green wool tunic to the knees over plain trousers, thick knitted stockings, the grey-white hair loose. She holds a clay cup of broth in both hands, a quiet, guarded look.
battle: Ready to loose: the grey-green deerskin shirt with leather bracers over the cuffs, the skinning knife at her belt. In her left hand she holds the yew longbow forward at full draw with an arrow nocked, the right hand at her cheek; the long lock across her forehead, the green eyes narrowed on a far target, the mouth closed.
formal: At the council fire of the White Hill: a straight-cut grey-green deerskin dress to the shins, rubbed soft and clean, with leather thongs lacing the sleeve ends and a plain hide belt, a short deer-hide cape over the shoulders pinned with a bone clasp. The white-haired yew bow is carried in her left hand, a thin green glow running through its wrapped grip. She stands with a straight back, a cool, formal look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the green eyes looking straight at the viewer with an icy, sharp calm, the long lock of grey-white hair across the brow, the lips closed. Cold blue forest-mist light from one side and a thin warm line of dusk light from the other. Foreground blur: drifting mist and a few dark pine needles. She wears the grey-green deerskin hunting shirt.

name: 伯德玛
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:363
who: Berdma, a human priestess of the Forest Sea, fifty-one, who still looks like a woman in her early forties: about 168 cm, full-figured and stately. Pale lavender hair in one thick braid hanging to the backs of the knees, oak leaves and fine silver chains woven into it, a few white strands at the temples. Pale amber eyes with the lids always half lowered, as if she has just woken from a dream or has not yet woken. A dignified, gentle face. A small grey ash mark painted on her forehead, the rule of the Forest Sea priests. A slow, soft, drowsy air; she walks slowly as if afraid of waking something.
build: 168 cm, full-figured and stately, soft shoulders, a full bust, a rounded waist and hips, a D-cup; she walks slowly.
palette: pale lavender and amber, undyed linen, deep walnut brown, oak-leaf green
casual: Her priestess clothes: a long undyed linen robe closed down the front with buttons, fitted sleeves, a deep walnut-brown wool cloak over it with a ring of dried acorns sewn along its edge, a leather pouch at her belt holding the burnt tips of twigs and a pinch of ash. In her right hand an oak staff with a small bone bell hanging from its head. The braid hangs in front over one shoulder.
private: At her cabin: a long-sleeved, high-collared soft undyed wool dress to the ankles, a knitted shawl, wool stockings on her feet, the braid coiled loosely. She holds a bundle of dried herbs in both hands, a drowsy, gentle look.
battle: Calling up a dream: the linen robe and brown cloak, the pouch open at her belt. She holds the oak staff up before her with both hands, the bone bell ringing, a burning twig glowing in the head of the staff, faint pale-violet smoke curling round her hands, the half-lidded amber eyes steady and calm.
formal: At the rites of the Forest Sea: a long clean undyed linen robe embroidered along the hem and cuffs with oak leaves in dark thread, the walnut-brown cloak pinned with a silver oak-leaf clasp, the braid freshly woven with new silver chains, the ash mark on the brow. She stands very still, the staff upright in her right hand, a calm, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the face large and slightly tilted, the half-lidded amber eyes looking at the viewer as if between waking and dream, the lips closed, a faint drowsy calm. Warm firelight from below the frame and a pale violet haze of smoke behind. Foreground blur: drifting ash and a few oak leaves. She wears the linen robe and the brown cloak with its ring of acorns.

name: 芬尼
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:558
who: Finny, an old human poet of Mirror Lake, seventy-four, who has spent seven years fishing for one silver-scaled salmon: about 174 cm, thin and long, a little stooped. A thin growth of white hair held back with a single reed, a long white beard hanging down over his chest. Very bright eyes that squeeze into a slit when he smiles. Fair skin, deeply lined. A chatty, cheerful, patient air; he hums old songs and keeps going when he loses the tune.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old man's face of seventy-four, thin, long and deeply lined, wrinkles fanning from the outer corners of the bright eyes and across the forehead and cheeks, thin white eyebrows, a long white beard; the eyes bright and narrow, squeezed shut into a slit by a broad smile; a long nose. Skin shadows are a soft warm tone.
build: 174 cm, thin and long, a little stooped.
palette: lake grey-blue and reed green, faded oatmeal, driftwood brown, silver-white
casual: His lakeside clothes: a long patched oatmeal wool robe belted with a cord, the sleeves wide, a grey wool shawl over his shoulders, plain trousers and worn leather shoes; a long wooden fishing rod in his right hand, a basket of birch bark hanging at his hip. A cheerful, squinting smile.
private: At home in his hut: a loose undyed wool shirt with the collar open and the sleeves pushed up, a thick knitted shawl, soft slippers. He holds a clay cup in both hands and hums, the eyes closed in a smile.
battle: He never fights and carries no weapon: the oatmeal robe hitched up through the belt, the grey shawl wrapped tight round his shoulders, he stands braced on both feet holding a bent fishing rod in both hands as if a great fish were pulling, the beard blowing, a rare fierce, laughing look.
battle_pose: 3) the lake outfit: braced and pulling, the knees bent, both hands gripping a bent fishing rod, the shoulders set, a fierce, delighted look; he never fights and holds no weapon.
formal: At a feast of the poets: a clean long robe of lake grey-blue wool with wide sleeves, tied with a narrow silver-grey cord belt, a small bunch of reeds pinned at the chest with a bone pin, a thin silver thread of lake-light running through the reeds, polished old shoes. He stands as straight as his stoop allows, hands clasped in front, a warm, mischievous smile.
art: A portrait with the camera slightly tilted, the face large, the bright eyes squeezed into a crinkled smile, the white beard falling across the front of his robe. Soft pale morning light off the lake from one side. Foreground blur: the tip of a fishing rod, a drifting reed and a single silver glint of a fish scale.

name: 柯马
src: 月银纪史诗/第五歌_冰矛抵眉.md:572
who: Koma, a human, High King of the White Hill, about forty: about 170 cm, not tall, steady and heavy in bearing. Dark hair cut short, a clean-shaven face, deep-set eyes of watchful grey and the quiet look of a man who has thought about the same thing twenty-three times. On his head a crown set with one glowing red core of fire, taken from the king of a flame-maned wolf pack he slew at twenty; the crown is a size too large for his head. A heavy, calm, grave air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a mature man's face of about forty, firm and square, a faint line between the brows and at the corners of the watchful grey eyes; straight dark eyebrows; a closed, level mouth. Fair, clean skin.
palette: royal crimson and dark grey, ember red, iron, deep blue-black
casual: His king's everyday clothes: a knee-length dark-grey wool tunic with long fitted sleeves, belted, over dark trousers and high leather boots, a heavy crimson wool cloak over one shoulder, the crown with its glowing red core on his head, a plain iron ring on one hand. He stands steady with the hands loosely at his sides.
private: Alone at night: a long-sleeved, high-collared undyed wool robe to the ankles, soft slippers, no cloak and no crown, the dark hair a little rumpled. A tired, thoughtful look.
battle: Ready to defend his city: a hide cuirass over the dark-grey tunic, an iron-reinforced leather cap under the crown, iron bracers, the crimson cloak pinned back. He grips a long straight sword in his right hand held forward and low, a heavy shield on his left arm; a grim, unflinching look.
formal: On the high seat of the White Hill, as kings of the beast age dress: the whole pelt of the great red beast his forefathers slew worn over the shoulders with its maned head on his right shoulder, the fur giving off a slow ember glow, the forepaws knotted across the chest and held with a big bronze pin, under it a straight-cut long tunic of undyed wool with a wide leather belt and antler toggles; the crown with the glowing red beast-core on his head, a staff of one whole bone in his right hand. He stands upright and grave, a stern, level look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face slightly turned, the grey eyes looking straight at the viewer with a heavy, patient calm, the lips closed, the oversized crown with its red core glowing against the shadow. Warm ember light from the crown on one side, cool dark stone behind. Foreground blur: drifting ash and a few red sparks.
